basics.name: Chenyu Gu
basics.label: M.S. in Bioengineering, Georgia Institute of Technology
basics.summary: M.S. student in Bioengineering at Georgia Tech (RoboMed Lab, advised by Dr. Jaydev Desai), working on the design, modeling, and control of medical continuum robots. My research spans medical and bio-robotics, surgical navigation and medical devices, and biomechanical/physiological sensing.

work.company: RoboMed Lab, Georgia Institute of Technology
work.summary: Design, modeling, and control of a hydraulically actuated continuum robot.
highlights: Developed and manufactured a polymer-based hydraulic robotic system for non-conductive, MRI-safe environments.
Formulated the physical model of the hydraulic robot and refined it with a data-driven hysteresis model.
Implemented model-based open-loop control and integrated shape-sensing methods for closed-loop control.
Characterized and validated the system experimentally and demonstrated it in a vascular phantom model.

work.company: RoboMed Lab, Georgia Institute of Technology
work.summary: Mechanism and actuation design of a steerable robotic guidewire (paper prepared for IJRR).
highlights: Contributed to a modified COAST robotic guidewire enabling active stiffness control for steering and quick-connect usability in minimally invasive cardiovascular interventions.
Managed the electrical development of the actuation system (PCB and circuit design) and developed an analog force sensor for precise robotic actuation and sensing.

work.company: Brain-robot Rehabilitation Lab, Southern University of Science and Technology
work.summary: Hardware/software co-design of a surgical navigation system.
highlights: Co-designed hardware and software, including circuit design to integrate microcontroller and sensors, C embedded programming, and real-time tracking feedback through Unity.
Validated effectiveness (validity and reliability) against an optical system and a robot arm.

work.company: Intelligent Heart Technology Lab, KTH Royal Institute of Technology
work.summary: Movement analysis using IMU sensors and sensor fusion.
highlights: Investigated the relationship between movement and cardiovascular function through gait parameters and heart rate.
Deployed a Kalman filter for orientation estimation, calibrated IMU angles, and extracted gait parameters and center of mass.

work.position: Project Leader — Motion Capture for Rehabilitation
work.company: Brain-robot Rehabilitation Lab, Southern University of Science and Technology
highlights: Integrated UWB technology and IMU to build a motion capture system for human motion recovery.
Developed Unity visualization and Python signal transmission, and applied deep learning for pose reconstruction.
Evaluated system effectiveness on healthy subjects during rehabilitation exercises.

work.position: Project Assistant — Center of Mass Estimation
work.company: Brain-robot Rehabilitation Lab, Southern University of Science and Technology
work.summary: Center of mass estimation for rehabilitation assessment.
highlights: Used IMU-based motion capture and developed an OpenSim-based algorithm to estimate the 3D center of mass.
Analyzed center-of-mass trajectories to extract motion features and perform rehabilitation assessments.

work.company: Dept. of Orthopedics, First People's Hospital, Shenzhen
work.summary: Clinical evaluation of medical measurement devices for orthopedic surgery.
highlights: Investigated suitable medical measurement devices to support orthopedic surgeries.
Performed clinical validation in the operating room and evaluated device functionality and reliability.

publications.name: Design and Modeling of a Polymer-based Hydraulic Continuum Robot for Minimal Invasive Surgery
publications.publisher: International Symposium on Medical Robotics (ISMR) — Accepted; Best Student Paper Award Finalist
publications.summary: A 2.14 mm-OD, MRI-compatible hydraulic continuum robot for minimally invasive surgery, with a Preisach hysteresis model (2.26 deg RMSE) and a 58.8% reduction in twisting, demonstrated in a 2D aortic-arch phantom.

publications.name: A Portable Inertial Navigation System for Total Hip Arthroplasty Targeting Direct Anterior Approach
publications.publisher: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement (IF: 5.9)
publications.summary: A wireless, radiation-free IMU-based navigation system quantifying acetabular cup orientation for the direct anterior approach, achieving 1.24 deg (RA) and 1.89 deg (RI) RMSE with CC > 0.995.

publications.name: IMU-based motion capture system for rehabilitation applications: A systematic review
publications.publisher: Biomimetic Intelligence and Robotics — Annual Best Paper Award (IF: 5.4)
publications.summary: A systematic review of 65 studies on IMU-based motion capture systems for rehabilitation, covering applications, sensor configurations, and future directions.
